source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Nematode (ណេម៉ាតូដ): nematodes are a common pest/pathogen of corn. Nematodes are microscopic worm-like organisms that can move through the pore spaces of soil particles. Symptoms and signs of this problem are that corn roots become discolored, brown, or show swollen/knotted lesions, causing plant growth to be stunted. This damage occurs both in water and in soil. Damage caused by nematodes together with appropriate environmental conditions can result in poor nutrient uptake by the crop.

Prevention and control measures include:
- Select land carefully for the crop.
- Practice crop rotation with other crop types.
- Use clean/pathogen-free seed lots, and destroy or remove infested plant residue.
